props.classMechanic_text:
HUNTER TUTORIAL — TRAPS

“Set the field. Force their move.”

What Are Traps?

Traps are prepped tools the Hunter unleashes to lock enemies in place, inflict statuses, and control the opening of a fight. You trade IP and MP for a burst of control that targets multiple creatures at once.

Deploy Timing: By default, you place a trap right before round 1. If your table uses a Surprise Round, you may instead ambush outside of combat (see Ambush Mode below).

Trap Sizes & Costs

Effect SizeIP CostMP CostTargets
MinorTrap [SL]5One creature
MediumTrap [SL]10Two creatures
MajorTrap [SL]15Three creatures

Your current Trap [SL] (skill level) sets the IP you must spend. MP scales with size.

How Traps Resolve

  1. Choose targets up to the size limit (1 / 2 / 3).
  2. Each target makes an Opposed Check: Target: DEX + INS vs Hunter: DEX + INS + [SL]
  3. On a success, a creature escapes your trap.
  4. On a failure, apply the trap’s effect (e.g., damage, poisoned, movement lock, etc.).

Note: Unless a trap says otherwise, you can only deploy it at the start of a conflict scene.

Ambush Mode (Optional Rule)

If your table uses the Surprise Round rule, you may place a trap to ambush unaware enemies before combat begins. If you do, you can’t also place a trap again at the normal “start of conflict” timing.

Design Tip: Ambush is best when you need an early status or to split a group before they cluster. Minor traps shine here—cheap, decisive, and safe.

Quick Reference

  • Pick an Effect Size (Minor / Medium / Major).
  • Spend IP = [SL] and the listed MP.
  • Select up to 1 / 2 / 3 targets in range.
  • Opposed Check: your DEX+INS+[SL] vs each target’s DEX+INS.
  • Apply effects to those who fail; others escape.

Hunter Tips

  • Open with Control: Use traps to lock key enemies while allies position.
  • Size for Budget: Minor is efficient; Major swings boss adds.
  • Synergize: Pair status traps with allies who exploit that status.
  • Mind Your MP: Medium/Major eat resources—plan recovery.

Worked Example

Example A — Medium Poison Dart Trap (SL 3): Before round 1, the Hunter spends 3 IP (Trap [SL]=3) and 10 MP to deploy a Medium Poison Dart Trap targeting two creatures.

Each target makes an Opposed Check: their DEX+INS vs the Hunter’s DEX+INS+3 (the +3 is from Trap [SL]=3).

One target fails and suffers [HR + 10] poison damage and the poisoned status, as per Poison Dart (SL 3). The other succeeds and escapes the trap with no effect.

Example B — Smoke Bomb (SL 1) with timing clause: At start of round, the Hunter spends 1 IP (Trap [SL]=1) and 5 MP to place a Minor Smoke Bomb covering two foes.

Each target rolls DEX+INS vs the Hunter’s DEX+INS+1. One target fails and is hit by the smoke: within a full round they suffer a -2 penalty to all Accuracy Checks. However, because that target had already taken a turn this round, the Smoke Bomb’s penalty begins at the start of the next round (per the trap’s timing rule).

props.class_lore: Hunters are masters of the wild — expert trackers, survivalists, and trappers who possess a deep understanding, respect, and connection to nature or the environment in which they specialize in hunting. They revere the cycle of life and often form a symbiotic bond with the creatures they hunt, utilizing the abilities and instincts of their quarry to enhance their own. While some Hunters prefer a nomadic life, others take root and become one with their habitat, whether natural, urban or rural. Therefore, the Hunter's prowess extends beyond the natural world and can be adapted to any terrain, from populous cities to desolate landscapes.
